# Specification

Declaring a command: its flags, valued options, positional arguments, subcommands and version.

<h2 id="option-spec"><code>OptionSpec</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct OptionSpec {
    pub name: char8[..];
    pub short: char32;
    pub value: char8[..];
    pub help: char8[..];
}
```

One option a command accepts, such as `--output FILE` or `-v`.
`Copy`; the text it holds is borrowed and must outlive the specification.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/CommandLine/Src/Spec.rux#L12)

**Fields**

| Name    | Type        | Description                                                                                           |
| ------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`  | `char8[..]` | The long name without its dashes, such as `output` for `--output`. Never empty.                       |
| `short` | `char32`    | The short name, such as `o` for `-o`, or `'\0'` for none. An ASCII letter or digit.                   |
| `value` | `char8[..]` | What the help text calls the option's value, such as `FILE`, or empty for a flag that takes no value. |
| `help`  | `char8[..]` | One line saying what the option does.                                                                 |

<h2 id="positional-kind"><code>PositionalKind</code></h2>

```rux
pub enum PositionalKind {
    Required,
    Optional,
    Remaining
}
```

How a positional argument may be given.
`Copy`, carrying no payload.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/CommandLine/Src/Spec.rux#L26)

**Cases**

| Name        | Description                                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Required`  | Exactly once; parsing fails without it.                                                                     |
| `Optional`  | At most once.                                                                                               |
| `Remaining` | Any number of times, taking every remaining positional argument. Only the last positional may be this kind. |

<h2 id="positional-spec"><code>PositionalSpec</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct PositionalSpec {
    pub name: char8[..];
    pub kind: PositionalKind;
    pub help: char8[..];
}
```

One positional argument a command accepts, such as `<input>`.
`Copy`; the text it holds is borrowed and must outlive the specification.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/CommandLine/Src/Spec.rux#L38)

**Fields**

| Name   | Type             | Description                                                           |
| ------ | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name` | `char8[..]`      | The name queries and the help text use, such as `input`. Never empty. |
| `kind` | `PositionalKind` | How the argument may be given.                                        |
| `help` | `char8[..]`      | One line saying what the argument is.                                 |

<h2 id="command-spec"><code>CommandSpec</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct CommandSpec {
    pub name: char8[..];
    pub summary: char8[..];
    pub version: char8[..];
    pub options: OptionSpec[..];
    pub positionals: PositionalSpec[..];
    pub commands: CommandSpec[..];
}
```

A command: what it is called, what it accepts, and the subcommands under it.
`Copy`; every slice and text it holds is borrowed and must outlive it and every parse made from it. A command with
subcommands takes the first positional argument as the subcommand's name, so it should declare no positionals of
its own.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/CommandLine/Src/Spec.rux#L52)

**Fields**

| Name          | Type                 | Description                                                                            |
| ------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`        | `char8[..]`          | The command's name: the program's name at the top, and the word that selects it below. |
| `summary`     | `char8[..]`          | One line saying what the command does.                                                 |
| `version`     | `char8[..]`          | The version `--version` reports, or empty when the command has none.                   |
| `options`     | `OptionSpec[..]`     | The options, in the order the help text lists them.                                    |
| `positionals` | `PositionalSpec[..]` | The positional arguments, in the order they are given.                                 |
| `commands`    | `CommandSpec[..]`    | The subcommands, in the order the help text lists them.                                |

**Methods**

<h2 id="flag"><code>Flag</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Flag(
    name: char8[..],
    short: char32,
    help: char8[..]
) -> OptionSpec
```

An option that is present or absent and takes no value, such as `--verbose`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/CommandLine/Src/Spec.rux#L73)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type        | Description                          |
| ------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `name`  | `char8[..]` | the long name without its dashes     |
| `short` | `char32`    | the short name, or `'\0'` for none   |
| `help`  | `char8[..]` | one line saying what the option does |

**Returns**: the option's specification

<h2 id="value-option"><code>ValueOption</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ValueOption(
    name: char8[..],
    short: char32,
    value: char8[..],
    help: char8[..]
) -> OptionSpec
```

An option that takes a value, such as `--output FILE`.
The value may follow the option as the next argument, after `=` in the long form, or directly after the short
letter, so `--output a.txt`, `--output=a.txt`, `-o a.txt` and `-oa.txt` all give `a.txt`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/CommandLine/Src/Spec.rux#L86)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type        | Description                                                     |
| ------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`  | `char8[..]` | the long name without its dashes                                |
| `short` | `char32`    | the short name, or `'\0'` for none                              |
| `value` | `char8[..]` | what the help text calls the value, such as `FILE`; never empty |
| `help`  | `char8[..]` | one line saying what the option does                            |

**Returns**: the option's specification

<h2 id="command"><code>Command</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Command(
    name: char8[..],
    summary: char8[..]
) -> CommandSpec
```

A command with a name and a summary, and as yet no version, options, positionals or subcommands.
The `With` methods fill in the rest, each returning the changed copy.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/CommandLine/Src/Spec.rux#L123)

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type        | Description                                               |
| --------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`    | `char8[..]` | the program's name, or the word that selects a subcommand |
| `summary` | `char8[..]` | one line saying what the command does                     |

**Returns**: the command's specification
